candidates.spoken_line: How did a NASA spacecraft fly straight through the Sun's million-degree atmosphere—without melting?
candidates.opening_visual: Real onboard WISPR white-light camera footage from Parker Solar Probe flying straight through glowing solar coronal streamers
candidates.rationale: Opens at 0.00s inside real onboard camera footage from inside the Sun's atmosphere paired with a direct 14-word thermal physics paradox.

candidates.spoken_line: Three point eight million miles from the Sun, NASA flew a camera inside million-degree plasma—and kept its instruments at room temperature.
candidates.opening_visual: NASA SDO AIA 304A extreme-ultraviolet solar prominence erupting off the blazing limb of the Sun
candidates.rationale: Contrasts blazing extreme-ultraviolet solar plasma with a 30°C room-temperature payload.

candidates.spoken_line: Why can an engineer touch the back of NASA's solar heat shield while its front faces the Sun's corona?
candidates.opening_visual: APL cleanroom engineers fitting the 4.5-inch octagonal carbon-foam Thermal Protection System onto Parker Solar Probe
candidates.rationale: Grounds the mystery immediately in tangible cleanroom spacecraft engineering.
